correctness.rationale: The missing s→t face enters each two-path boundary with the same nonzero ξ coefficient, so full invariance is exactly the augmentation kernel in degree two: the second boundary is a zero-chain and there are no further restrictions. On the two trivial mean-branch lines D1 has rank two, leaving one trivial vertex line. On the U_m blocks in degrees 2,1,0, D2 is v↦(ξ²v,v) and D1 is (a,b)↦a+ξb. For N≥3 their composition ξ(1+ξ) is nonzero; thus the chain splits into a length-three U_m string plus an isolated middle U_m. The trivial part is two length-two strings and one isolated degree-zero line. A length-ℓ string contributes at a position iff fewer than q steps lead downward and fewer than N−q lead upward. This gives all three displayed tables, including disjoint cases for N=3 and q=2. For N=2 the U_m part instead has two length-two strings; all length-two strings are acyclic at q=1, leaving only the isolated trivial degree-zero line. Symbolic verification over C is decisive; 8·(1+⋯+7)=224 archived modular cases only corroborate dimensions, not modules.
